(i) low-level postoperative troponins predict long-term mortality, but (ii) they are not associated with typical cardiac symptoms or ECG changes, and (iii) higher postoperative tropons are associated with cardiac symptoms and ECG changes, but they are also associated with long-term mortality.

postoperative tropons are associated with a continuum of cardiac injury ranging from subclinical myocardial injury to overt myocardial infarctions.

postoperative cardiac complications are uncommon and that postoperative tro- poni n e elevations, even low-level elevations, are common and strongly associated with postoperative mortality.
